# A09-S48: Correspondence

Correspondence extract. [████] marks redaction; […] marks omission.

[…]
I read that he is running as an independent and only needs to collect/recommend by 150 and at most 200 voters to be an independent. Should we try that – it seems much more manageable – but do you want to sit in the Folketing? And you can only, if Leder Lars either gets CPR and citizenship – or you run yourself and have your mentor with you 😃

Running outside the parties
If you run as a candidate outside the parties, it is popularly called being an independent.
Before you can run outside the parties, you must be recommended by at least 150 and at most 200 voters. The signatures must be sent to the Appeals Board when the election is called.
You can get into the Folketing by receiving 15.000-20.000 personal votes in a large constituency and thereby 1 a constituency mandate.
It has only happened twice since 1953 that an independent was elected to the Folketing. Most recently it was Jacob Haugaard, who in 1994 got 23.253 personal votes. Getting into the Folketing as an independent is thus a difficult way to be elected.
Regarding being nervous about who shows up, they have to reveal themselves when they sign up and then we have to take our precautions – there are certainly several bad characters [████] So we take a risk … therefore I also think it is good to have paid registration and a guard at the door…

And then we need to prepare some answers – that is important!
